subject: Next steps: Concurrency & burst profile for Acme AI POC
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acmeai.com>, Sam Cho <scho@acmeai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & data request from today

Hi Priya / Sam —

Thanks for the productive call today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff: 

Summary of agreed success criteria (please confirm / edit):
- Functional: Redwood must serve API responses consistent with your model outputs; no functional regressions vs your baseline.
- Performance: p95 latency < 200ms, p99 latency < 350ms under expected concurrency for the POC; 95% of single-request completions within these targets.
- Stability: No more than 1% error rate (5xx/timeout) during a 48hr sustained run.
- Cost guardrail: Provide estimated token cost envelope for the two-week trial (we'll provide rough cost numbers).
- Evaluation: Run your canonical prompt set (attached template) and a short production-like traffic replay; results to be shared in a readout.

To size the environment and build the test plan we need the following workload inputs from your side (attached are sample CSV schema and a template trace):
1) Baseline and peak RPS ranges (typical, expected peak, and anticipated maximum burst)
2) Concurrency (clients/threads) you expect hitting the endpoint concurrently
3) Token length distributions: prompt tokens (mean/95th) and completion tokens (mean/95th) or representative samples
4) Burst shape examples: duration, ramp, and frequency (e.g., 10–15 min bursts, hourly spikes)
5) A sample 24–48hr request trace or a small synthetic trace (CSV) we can replay
6) Any rate-limiting or client-side backoff behavior we should replicate

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Priya: share a 24–48hr trace + canonical prompts by Tue, Jun 29 (attachment: template).
- Redwood: map to instance selection, propose initial concurrency targets and a POC schedule by Wed, Jun 30.
- Ops kickoff call: propose Tue, Jul 6 or Wed, Jul 7 (30 minutes) — confirm your preference.

Owners: 
- Michael Grant (me): POC owner, primary contact, overall success criteria and readout.
- Lauren Bishop: Customer ops, will run the load harness and telemetry collection.
- Aditya Rao: ML infra lead, model variant selection and quantization recommendations.

Attachments: [Attachment: acme_success_criteria.md (Markdown, 6KB)]

Thanks — looking forward to getting the traces and locking the kickoff.

Best,
Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acmeai.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Cho <scho@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & data request from today

Thanks Michael — quick answers below and attached a small sample trace (24h subset). Let me know if you need a longer window.

Workload inputs:
- Typical baseline: 12 RPS sustained during business hours (09:00–18:00 PT).
- Expected peaks: hourly micro-spikes up to ~60 RPS for short (1–2 min) bursts when queued jobs finish.
- Burst scenarios: a traffic-surge pattern when bulk previews complete — we see 90–140 RPS for 5–12 minute windows, roughly 2–3 times per day during batch runs.
- Concurrency: our frontend maintains 8–12 simultaneous client connections for generation calls during peak.
- Token lengths (observed):
  - Prompt tokens: mean 32, p95 ~78
  - Completion tokens: mean 110, p95 ~310
  - Combined mean roundtrip tokens ~142
- Typical timeout/backoff: clients retry twice with exponential backoff starting at 250ms; we can disable retries for the POC to measure raw behavior.

Attachments: [Attachment: acme_sample_trace.csv (CSV, 92KB)]

Success criteria: the numbers you proposed above look fine to us. One ask: please include a cost projection in your POC readout (tokens/hour x projected cost) so we can justify to finance.

Kickoff: Jul 6 (Tue) works for us for the ops kickoff. 30 minutes preferred.

Priya
VP Product
Acme AI

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acmeai.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: POC plan & owner assignments

Looping up internal next steps based on Priya's trace and the targets she confirmed:

Plan sketch (internal):
- Environment: start with two dedicated endpoints (medium GPU profile) and a shared burst pool for short spikes. We'll size further after an initial dry-run.
- Load harness: I'll run a 24hr replay of the attached trace to collect baseline p95/p99 and error rates.
- Canary policy: configure progressive ramp with auto-fallback to a smaller model variant if p99 > 500ms during sustained load.
- Telemetry: enable token-level billing traces, request/response latency histograms, and per-client error breakdown.

Action items and owners:
- Lauren: run trace replay + produce baseline report by Fri, Jul 2. (Deliverable: baseline_report.md and raw telemetry exports)
- Aditya: produce initial model/quantization recommendation and a resource map (vCPU/GPU, memory) by Fri, Jul 2. (Deliverable: resource_map.pdf)
- Michael: finalize acceptance criteria & coordinate kickoff calendar invite for Jul 6. (Deliverable: POC schedule + readout template)

Timeline:
- Jul 2: Baseline and resource recommendations in hand.
- Jul 6: Ops kickoff call (30m) to validate runbook and start the first week of runs.
- Jul 6–20: 2-week POC run (rolling readouts every 3 days).
- Jul 21: Readout & decision meeting.

Notes: Priya asked for a concise cost projection — include token/hour and 2-week projected spend in the baseline report. Also add a short checklist to the kickoff doc for any client-side opt-outs (disable retries).

--Lauren
Director, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
